claims.text: Adding approximately 1–2 at.% boron to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding approximately 1–2 at.% boron will enhance the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
The beneficial effect requires boron to be within a narrow concentration window of approximately 1–2 at.%.
The beneficial effect requires rapid-solidification processing.
Boron contents substantially outside the proposed 1–2 at.% window may eliminate the benefit.
Deviations in processing conditions, such as cooling rate, may eliminate the benefit of boron addition.
Boron atoms are small relative to the relevant alloy constituents.
Minor boron addition will promote tighter local atomic packing.
Minor boron addition will increase chemical heterogeneity in the liquid and glassy structures.
Minor boron addition will increase topological heterogeneity in the liquid and glassy structures.
Boron-induced structural changes will enhance short-to-medium-range order.
Enhanced short-to-medium-range order will deepen potential-energy minima.
The proposed structural and energetic changes will suppress crystallization kinetics.
Suppression of crystallization kinetics will stabilize the amorphous matrix.
The boron-added alloy will have a greater critical casting thickness than the otherwise comparable boron-free alloy.
The boron-added alloy will have a higher DSC crystallization temperature than the otherwise comparable boron-free alloy.
The boron-free baseline presently has relatively lower critical casting thickness.
The boron-free baseline presently has relatively lower thermal stability.
